open_comment_speakers.name: Mary Louise Chavers
open_comment_speakers.topic: Chemical sensitivity is a very serious issue and would encourage the City to pursue other avenues rather than pesticide fogging Believes that larvicide's are a more effective

open_comment_speakers.name: Steven Ross
open_comment_speakers.topic: Lazydog and the brick façade. Mr. Ross had a great experience with the City staff throughout the remodel but has been very disappointed with the time it has taken to resolve the brick issue

open_comment_speakers.name: Patrick Murphy
open_comment_speakers.topic: Dogs off leash are a hazard and nuisance Believes dogs off leash create environmental damage

open_comment_speakers.name: Rob Smoke
open_comment_speakers.topic: Suggests bringing the discussion to the table of pocket parks at the 29 th St site

open_comment_speakers.name: Tim Thomas
open_comment_speakers.topic: Pedestrian crossing at San Juan Del Centro. Concerned about the safety of pedestrians in this area

open_comment_speakers.name: Robert Temple Frost
open_comment_speakers.topic: Asks Council to investigate the conversion of organic waste into diesel fuel as a revenue source for the City.

open_comment_speakers.name: Lisa Morzel
open_comment_speakers.topic: Concerned about the pedestrian crossing at Valmont and 34 th Watched for 45 minutes and believes this crosswalk to be highly used by the residence of San Juan Del Centro but in serious need of maintenance.

open_comment_speakers.name: Arturo Martinez
open_comment_speakers.topic: Students and the professor from the University of Chapingo visiting Boulder OSMP Very impressed with Boulders balance of wildlife, agricultural and human existence.

open_comment_speakers.name: Ben Binder
open_comment_speakers.topic: In favor of downtown kiosk but concerned about the use by some businesses Suggests an Ordinance to help control those that place multiple flyers all over the kiosks

open_comment_speakers.name: Jim Haswell
open_comment_speakers.topic: Disc Golf needs a place to play They voluntarily moved their teams from a local park when the user conflicts became to high and are now hoping for City support to have a place at Valmont Park Recommended site PDGA.com

open_comment_speakers.name: Alexander Holcomb
open_comment_speakers.topic: No magnesium Chloride on the bike paths, please It remains slick for days 2 Not in favor of electronic voting on any level. 3. Seeking council support of an 18 hole disc golf course within the City

open_comment_speakers.name: Lynn Segal
open_comment_speakers.topic: Expressed concerns over long term issues, such as housing, retail and pocket parks at 29 th St.

open_comment_speakers.name: Dalene Beaver
open_comment_speakers.topic: Concerned about kiosks on the mall Would like to see a maximum of 2 notices per organization enforced and no posting over others material Also feels that monitoring of removal of information is important

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Toor moved, seconded by McGrath to approve consent items 3A through 4H

Councilmember Eldridge moved, seconded by Riggle to adopt Ordinance No 7351 amending Title 9, “Land Use Regulation,” B R C 1981, by changing the regulations for floor area ratios in the RB1-X zoning district to permit additional housing within the downtown by allowing the existing 0.5 floor area ratio exclusion for above grade parking to also be used for residential uses.

Councilmember McGrath moved, seconded by Riggle to approve #2 of this item only with the stipulation to take steps to remain consistent with recommendations of SRT with conditions coming back to Council before final acceptance.
Councilmember Riggle moved, seconded by Eldridge to call-up the Landmark Alteration Certificate for 1346 Pearl Street
There being no further business to come before Council at this time, BY MOTION REGULARLY ADOPTED, THE MEETING WAS ADJOURNED AT 8:50P M
